[RFCS.23.2] **One typed-value encoding for facts and calls.** Every value is
an `Arg` (`proto/fact_external.proto#Arg`): a name, a `Kind`, and the one
value member that kind names (none for `KIND_NULL`). `Kind`
(`proto/fact_external.proto#Kind`) is one number space with two subtypes:

- a **slot value** admits the common kinds and `KIND_FACT_REF`;
- a **call argument** admits the common kinds and `KIND_ENCODED_FACT`.

A number belonging to one subtype is reserved in the other ([STYL.2.8.7]). So a
`FactExternal`'s fields never carry `KIND_ENCODED_FACT`, and a call's arguments
([RFCS.15.2]) never carry `KIND_FACT_REF`. A call argument never carries `KIND_NULL` in this edition: a call whose argument has no value is not made ([LNUL.11.1]). A `Json` value is the JSON text
[LGRA.5.8.7a] gives it.

A `Kind` is how a value is represented, not the type it was declared with. A
`Time`, `Date` or `Duration` value is `KIND_INT`, carrying the integer
[RDSC.5.5.8] gives it. A program that receives one reads it as its own slot's
declared type, which [RFCS.23.3] makes the writer's.

The engine's own slot-kind and argument-kind enumerations, and every other
consumer's, are generated from `Kind` and reconciled against it ([STYL.5.9.7]).
